podcast.title: MySpace for Direct Fan Engagement
podcast.body: While not discovered on MySpace, Panic! at the Disco effectively utilized the platform to directly reach fans, bypassing traditional gatekeepers like radio, record stores, and video channels, and enabling real-time interaction. "Panic was able to bypass radio, bypass record stores, bypass video channels and all the old guard and take their music directly to the fans efficiently and instantly."

podcast.title: Opposition to Trump Campaign Music Use
podcast.body: Panic! At The Disco was among a long list of artists who expressed strong opposition to Donald Trump's campaign using their music at political rallies. Despite venues often holding blanket performing rights licenses, artists did not want their work associated with the campaign and many pursued cease and desist orders or lawsuits. "The list of artists against Trump using their music is long."

podcast.title: Pop Punk Decline (2010s)
podcast.body: Despite the general decline of pop punk in the early 2010s, Panic! At The Disco, among other bands, persisted in the genre. "It never went away. I mean, we still had bands like Green Day and the offspring and Blink 2 and Panic at the disco."

podcast.title: Shift Towards Pop
podcast.body: In response to the prevalence of pure pop in the late 2000s, Panic! at the Disco also chose to "err on the side of pop when it came to writing new tunes." This decision reflected a move towards more mainstream pop trends in their songwriting. "This was the direction taken by Fallout Boy and Panic at the Disco."

xref.title: Dan Wilson's Songwriting Prowess
xref.body: Guitarist and singer Dan Wilson has achieved considerable recognition as a highly sought-after professional songwriter. He co-wrote Adele's massive global hit "Someone Like You," which topped charts in dozens of countries and earned him a Grammy for Song of the Year. He also received a Grammy for his production work on Adele's "21" album and was nominated for a Grammy for writing "Not Ready to Make Nice" for the Dixie Chicks. His extensive songwriting credits include collaborations with dozens of other notable acts, such as Fantagram, John Legend, Steve Perry, Josh Groban, Jason Barraiz, Leanne Rhyme, Stevie Nick's Halsey Cold War Kids, K-Flay, Weezer, Panic at the Disco, and Taylor Swift. "But the big story here is guitarist and singer Dan Wilson. He's become a renowned songwriter for hire."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Great Alt-Rock One-Hit Wonders of the 90s: Part 1

xref.title: Influence on Pop Punk
xref.body: Blink-182 is considered one of the most influential pop punk bands of the 21st century. Their style and career trajectory have left a significant mark on numerous artists across the genre, inspiring bands like Sum 41, Good Charlotte, Simple Plan, Panic! At The Disco, Fall Out Boy, Hedley, Billy Talent, You Me At Six, and Paramore. "Blink has to be considered one of the most influential pop punk bands of the 21st century."
